title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Nvidia Sends a Clean Set After Tuesday's Wipeout
conditions.summary: Stock futures are bouncing after Tuesday's sharp selloff, led by tech after Nvidia's strong results and outlook. Treasury yields above five percent, falling gold and oil, and the FOMC minutes this afternoon keep the water choppy.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 futures were up about 0.6% and Nasdaq-100 futures about 1.2% shortly before 5 AM ET; Dow futures rose about 0.3% and Russell 2000 futures about 0.2%.
The bounce follows a rough Tuesday: the S&P 500 fell about 1%, the Dow lost more than 800 points (-1.6%) and the Nasdaq slipped 0.7%.
The 10-year Treasury yield eased about 3 basis points to roughly 5.10%, still above the 5% line it crossed last week.
The dollar dipped about 0.2% after touching a 19-month high Tuesday; WTI crude fell about 1% to near $84, and gold dropped about 2.5% to a 14-month low near $3,766.
Bitcoin traded near $64,000, slightly lower, and the VIX eased to about 24 from Tuesday's higher levels.
Asia: MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan slipped 0.1% for a fifth straight loss and the Nikkei fell 0.3% after giving up early gains.
Europe: after Tuesday's worst session since March (Stoxx 600 -1.8%, DAX -2.1%), markets were steadier early Wednesday.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 7:30 AM CT: October housing starts and building permits.
9:00 AM CT: October pending home sales.
12:00 PM CT: 20-year Treasury bond auction, closely watched with yields above 5%.
1:00 PM CT: Minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting, where rates held at 3.75%-4.00% and two officials dissented in favor of a hike.
Fed speakers: Governor Barr at 12:35 PM CT, New York Fed President Williams at 1:30 PM CT and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari at 3:15 PM CT.
Main story: markets price a December rate hike as nearly certain, and a high-rate backdrop is weighing on gold, bitcoin and oil at the same time as AI stocks try to steady.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Nvidia (after Tuesday's close): fiscal Q3 revenue of about $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago, and adjusted EPS of $2.68 both topped estimates.
Nvidia guided Q4 revenue to about $130 billion, above the roughly $125 billion analysts expected, and approved another $150 billion for buybacks; shares rose about 3% pre-market.
Interim CEO Colette Kress said chip demand remains strong; the board said it does not plan to bring back Jensen Huang, who resigned last week.
Klarna: Q3 revenue of about $1.01 billion beat, but its adjusted loss per share was wider than expected; shares were little changed.
Before the open today: Target, TJX and Lowe's; early indications were thin at publication time.
After the close: Palo Alto Networks, expected to earn $0.97 per share on about $3.31 billion in revenue.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: NVDA (Nvidia): +3% — beat-and-raise quarter with a Q4 outlook above estimates.
NBIS (Nebius): +8% — AI cloud names rallied on the Nvidia report.
CRWV (CoreWeave): +6.5% — same AI cloud read-through from Nvidia.
MRVL (Marvell): +4.4% — chip stocks followed Nvidia higher; AMD, Micron and Broadcom also gained 2.5% to 3.4%.
CAPR (Capricor): +5% — ahead of Sunday's FDA decision date for its Duchenne muscular dystrophy therapy.
ASTS (AST SpaceMobile): +4% — bouncing after hitting a 52-week low Tuesday amid concerns over its rocket costs and timeline.
AAOI (Applied Optoelectronics): -4.7% — filed to sell up to $550 million of common stock.
INTC (Intel): +1.8% — on reports of fresh layoffs.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic is set to price its IPO this evening, seeking a valuation of up to about $1.4 trillion, with trading expected Thursday; it is seen as a test of investor appetite for AI.
Nvidia's leadership remains in focus after Jensen Huang's resignation last week; the board says it has no plans to reinstate him despite a campaign for his return.
Alibaba is under scrutiny over a controversy involving Nvidia chips and Megaspeed; its shares were roughly flat pre-market.
In Europe, Italian rocket maker Avio jumped Tuesday on a takeover offer from satellite company Iceye, while SAP and ASML each fell more than 5%.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: Whether the Nvidia-led bounce in futures holds through the 8:30 AM CT open after Tuesday's 800-point Dow drop.
The 20-year auction at noon CT and the FOMC minutes at 1:00 PM CT, with the 10-year yield sitting near 5.10%.
Palo Alto Networks after the close and Anthropic's IPO pricing tonight.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Wednesday, November eighteenth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. My trusty co-anchor Gus the wonder dog is sitting on the cabana deck with his ears up. Let them hear you, Gus! Alright, let's check the swell. Yesterday was a gnarly wipeout. The Dow dropped more than eight hundred points, and the S and P five hundred fell about one percent. But this morning on Dawn Patrol, the water looks better. S and P futures are up about six tenths of a percent. Nasdaq futures are up about one point two percent. Dow futures are up about three tenths, and the Russell is up a touch. The ten year Treasury yield eased about three basis points, to around five point one percent. Gold fell about two and a half percent to a fourteen month low. Crude slipped about one percent, to near eighty four dollars. Bitcoin is near sixty four thousand dollars. Over in Asia, stocks drifted a little lower. Europe is steadier after its worst day since March. Now, wind and weather. Housing starts come out at seven thirty A M Central. Pending home sales follow at nine. A twenty year Treasury auction hits at noon. Then the big one, the Fed minutes at one P M Central. Traders see a December rate hike as nearly locked in. Fed speakers Barr, Williams and Kashkari also paddle out this afternoon. On the tide chart, Nvidia was the big Kahuna last night. Revenue more than doubled to about one hundred sixteen billion dollars, and the outlook topped estimates. Nvidia is up about three percent before the bell. That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Target, T J X and Lowe's report before the open, and Palo Alto Networks reports after the close. In the lineup, A I cloud names are hanging ten. Nebius is up eight percent, and CoreWeave is up about six and a half. Marvell, A M D, Micron and Broadcom are riding the same wave. Capricor is up five percent ahead of an F D A decision. AST SpaceMobile bounced four percent off a yearly low. Applied Optoelectronics dropped nearly five percent on a stock sale. And Intel is up almost two percent on layoff reports. On beach talk, Anthropic is set to price its I P O tonight, at a value of up to one point four trillion dollars. Everybody will be watching that big swell. Sets to watch: whether this bounce holds at the open, the Fed minutes at one P M Central, and that I P O tonight. Want my read on a wave? Look up any stock, E T F or futures contract in the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
